entry.title: Matthew Dear, Armand Hammer, and More: This Week’s Pitchfork Selects Playlist
entry.summary: Our weekly playlist highlights songs that our writers, editors, and contributors are listening to on repeat
entry.content:
The staff of Pitchfork listens to a lot of new music. A lot of it. On any given day our writers, editors, and contributors go through an imposing number of new releases, giving recommendations to each other and discovering new favorites along the way. Each Monday, with our Pitchfork Selects playlist, we’re sharing what our writers are playing obsessively and highlighting some of the Pitchfork staff’s favorite new music. The playlist is a grab-bag of tracks: Its only guiding principle is that these are the songs you’d gladly send to a friend.

This week’s Pitchfork Selects playlist features Armand Hammer, Esther Rose, Matthew Dear and more. Listen below and follow our playlists on Apple Music and Spotify. (Pitchfork earns a commission from purchases made through affiliate links on our site.)

entry.title: Director of MGMT’s “Kids” and “Time to Pretend” Videos Dies at 43
entry.summary: Filmmaker Ray Tintori also shot videos for Solange, Arcade Fire, and the Killers
entry.content:
Ray Tintori, the filmmaker behind MGMT’s breakout Oracular Spectacular videos, has died, People and TMZ report. He was 43. No cause was provided, and his death is under investigation, according to both publications, citing the New York City Office of Chief Medical Examiner.

Born into a filmmaking family, Tintori started making shorts—Jettison Your Loved Ones and his award-winning thesis film Death to the Tinman—in the mid 2000s, before his break with the music videos for MGMT’s “Time to Pretend,” “Electric Feel,” and “Kids.” His fantastical sets and special effects dovetailed with a cozy, handmade feel that characterized his ongoing work. The “Kids” video starred Joanna Newsom as a mother oblivious to the writhing monsters that pursued her terrified toddler. (A behind-the-scenes short put to bed some lingering questions over whether the experience was a little harsh on the real-life toddler.) Tintori returned to work with MGMT on his final video, for the band’s Christine and the Queens collaboration “Dancing in Babylon.”

In the meantime, Tintori notched up a résumé that included the Killers’ “Spaceman,” Arcade Fire’s “Chemistry,” and Chairlift’s perpetually melting “Evident Utensil” visual. He contributed to the acclaimed magical realist drama Beasts of the Southern Wild, a product of the Court 13 collective he co-founded. Last year, Tintori co-directed a New York stage production of Ethan Coen’s Waiting and cameoed as a newsreel photographer in Marty Supreme.

entry.title: Superchunk Set 2027 North American Tour
entry.summary: New Merge signee Tanner York will support the band on the spring run
entry.content:
Superchunk have announced a 2027 North American tour, set to launch next spring. The trek, which New York-based power pop artist Tanner York is opening for, begins in Norfolk, Virginia on March 12 and concludes with a homecoming show in Carrboro, North Carolina on March 27. That final date will also include Lambchop.

After they conclude the North American run, Superchunk will head to Japan to play five shows across Hiroshima, Osaka, Nagoya, and Tokyo. The band shared their most recent album, Songs in the Key of Yikes, in 2025.

entry.title: Big Thief Plots 2027 U.S. Tour

entry.title: Chuquimamani-Condori Drops Some Folky Kelela Edits
entry.summary: “This is my ayni to you Kelela, an unpayable debt for your generosity”
entry.content:
After posting adorable photos of them cheesing together at C2C Festival, Chuquimamani-Condori has shared a folder of Kelela edits. Available for free, the zip file (which you can download at this link) includes Andean folk renditions of songs from 2026’s New Avatar, 2023’s Raven, and 2018’s Take Me Apart. The collection also offers a guitar-forward take on a deconstructed club single from 2016, when the two got together for “Reference Track TF Scrape.”

“Sharing some Kelela edits from old DJ sets over the years,” the musician wrote in an Instagram post. “This is my ayni to you Kelela, an unpayable debt for your generosity.” Chuquimamani-Condori has also been generous this year. In April, as one-half of the duo Los Thuthanaka, they released Wak’a, which followed another EP of mash-ups, Luzmila Edits.

Read Pitchfork’s feature The Music That Made Kelela.

entry.title: Big Thief, Death Cab for Cutie, Remi Wolf to Play Green River Fest 2027
entry.summary: This is Lorelei, Star Moles, Built to Spill, and Julia Jacklin are also booked for the western Massachusetts weekender in June
entry.content:
The lineup for the 2027 Green River Festival in Greenfield, Massachusetts has landed, led by headliners Big Thief, Death Cab for Cutie, and Remi Wolf. Set to take over the Franklin County Fairgrounds from June 18 through 20, the wider lineup features This is Lorelei, Julia Jacklin, Built to Spill, Star Moles, Jess Williamson, Slow Pulp, and Sylvan Esso. Check out the full bill below.

Next year will mark Green River Festival’s 41st annual edition. The three-day event is split up across three stages: the Back Porch Stage, the Dean’s Beans Stage, and the Round House Stage, the latter of which is reserved for local western Massachusetts artists. Green River’s 2026 edition was headlined by Charley Crockett, Spoon, and Geese, with J Mascis, Kurt Vile and the Violators, Wednesday, and Hurray for the Riff Raff appearing further down the bill.

entry.title: Jason Isbell and the 400 Unit Join Up With Drive-By Truckers for 2027 Tour
entry.summary: They’ll be trucking across the U.S. between May and September next year
entry.content:
Jason Isbell and the 400 Unit have locked in a joint 2027 headlining tour with Drive-By Truckers. Kicking off next May in Nashville, the run will bring the two bands around the U.S. through the fall, closing out with a show in Tulsa, Oklahoma on September 7. Get into a full itinerary below.

The Summer of Joy tour is a homecoming of sorts for Isbell, who was a member of Drive-By Truckers between 2001 and 2007. Isbell last reconnected with the band in October, when he joined them for a full set at his Alabama festival ShoalsFest. They also linked up in December 2025, when they performed “Hell No, I Ain’t Happy” from 2003’s Decoration Day on an episode of The Late Show With Stephen Colbert.

Isbell and the 400 Unit wrapped up their most recent tour back in July. In September, he also sued the AI company Suno alongside a cohort of musicians, alleging that the platform generated music based on their names without express permission.

entry.title: Julien Baker Lines Up New Album This World or the Next
entry.summary: “Hound” leads the singer-songwriter’s first solo album in five years
entry.content:
After years of high-profile collaborations, Julien Baker is back with a new solo album. This World or the Next is due February 12, via Matador. Self-produced and made with longtime collaborators Matt Gilliam and Calvin Lauber, the follow-up to 2021’s Little Oblivions embraces a heavier sound in evidence on new song “Hound.” Watch the Joshua Cannon-directed video for that below. “It feels like something we’ve been grasping at for a long time,” Baker said in a statement. “Making this music, it was like discovering people who spoke your own personal language.”

Baker’s star has, if anything, risen since that last solo LP. As well as their much-garlanded stint with Phoebe Bridgers and Lucy Dacus as Boygenius, they teamed up with Torres last year for a country album called Send a Prayer My Way.

entry.title: Ryley Walker Announces Tour and First Album in Six Years
entry.summary: “Cloud of Beaujolais” portends the Course in Fable follow-up, Darkening the Glass
entry.content:
On the heels of his return to the studio and signing to AD 93, Ryley Walker has lined up his first album since 2021’s Course in Fable. Darkening the Glass, out February 26, will be backed by a tour of North America and Europe from March through May. New song “Cloud of Beaujolais,” which follows the September comeback single “Carrier,” is out today, with an Emma Smith-directed video shot inside a manual car wash, if you’re into that sort of thing. Scroll down for the tour dates.

In a press release, Walker shared an anecdote about writing “Cloud of Beaujolais,” his final addition to the LP. “I sat in a chair with my forehead on the kitchen counter for the whole afternoon while I fleshed it out,” he said. “I got a big line on my forehead and everybody kept asking, ‘What’s wrong with your forehead?’ I said it was eczema because I didn’t want to admit I’d written a song. A pretty inept feeling. Andrew Young and Bill MacKay play beautifully on this.”

Walker has charted a more collaborative course since Course in Fable, working with the likes of James K, Joanne Robertson, Steve Gunn, and Chris Corsano. The new record features assorted players and production contributors including the aforementioned Young and MacKay, Ben Kudler, Max Allison, and Cooper Crain.

entry.title: Hayley Williams-Curated Outbreak Fest Features Dinosaur Jr., Blood Orange
entry.summary: Also: Mannequin Pussy, Rico Nasty, Ear, Soul Glo, and, yes, Hayley Williams
entry.content:
Hayley Williams is adding festival curator to her C.V. The Paramore singer, who is currently on tour in South America, was asked to choose the lineup for next year’s Outbreak Fest in Manchester. Among her selections: Dinosaur Jr., Blood Orange, Wednesday, American Football, Julien Baker, Mannequin Pussy, Rico Nasty, Ear, Soul Glo, and Feeble Little Horse. Williams will also headline both nights. You can check out the full poster and lineup below. The two-day event takes place on June 19 and 20 at B.E.C. Arena.

“Downright blasphemous to let me do this but its gonna be a good time and fucking rival schools,” Williams wrote on Instagram about curating the 15-year-old hardcore and punk event, which has recently expanded to other genres. A portion of proceeds from each ticket to the 2027 edition will be donated to Medical Aid For Palestinians, Not A Phase, and Manchester Central Foodbank.

In addition to the tour (her second of the year), Williams has spent 2026 debuting a new side project, Powersnatch. She was also, mere hours before the Outbreak announcement, nominated for a Best Alternative Music Performance Grammy for “Showbiz,” off 2025’s Ego Death at a Bachelorette Party.

entry.title: TV on the Radio to Headline Music Hall of Williamsburg’s Final Shows
entry.summary: The Brooklyn stalwarts will bring the curtain down once and for all on December 5 and 6
entry.content:
It feels only right that a band of Williamsburg stalwarts will see off the Williamsburg stalwart that is the (aptly named) Music Hall of Williamsburg. On December 5 and 6, TV on the Radio are set to headline the storied venue’s final two shows. A “very limited” number of tickets will be sold at the box office this Saturday, November 21, beginning at noon. Check out the poster below.

“It is truly only with the benefit of hindsight that we can appreciate what a special time and place Williamsburg in the early 2000s was,” reads a statement shared by TV on the Radio, who last played the Music Hall in 2014. “At the time, Interpol, the YYYs, Blonde Redhead, etc. were perhaps standouts, but not SO different from the myriad of lesser-known bands like Secret Machines, Fluxx Services Inc. or Tadanoshin, who were part of a rich local music and social scene that now seems ‘uniquely,’ but at the time just seemed ‘appropriately,’ creative.”

The band continues, “We didn’t realize that the institutions that fostered this creativity, including Music Hall of Williamsburg in its previous life as North Six, along with Galapagos, Death By Audio, the Stinger Club, Trash Bar, etc., would be so fleeting. Now the creative landscape of Williamsburg is entirely ‘different’ (cough cough), and it is with an extreme amount of melancholic reverence that we are saying goodbye to one of the last remaining vestiges of a community that naively nurtured genre-defining artists and sadly, because of its success, has been exploited out of existence.”

“Thank you, MHOW,” they conclude, “for being the site of so many great memories for us and for being part of the essential fabric of a truly special time and place. May the luxury condos be just as fleeting.”

Opened in 2007 at 66 North Sixth Street—previous residence of the rock club Northsix—Music Hall of Williamsburg was bought by entertainment conglomerate AEG in 2017. Last December, Music Hall’s operator, Bowery Presents, announced that the building’s owner had declined to renew their lease and the venue would be shuttering its doors at the end of this year. LCD Soundsystem, Julia Jacklin, and Lucy Dacus are among the other acts booked for the final few weeks.

Read about TV on the Radio’s Desperate Youth, Blood Thirsty Babes at No. 20 in Pitchfork’s new list of The 100 Best Indie Rock Albums of All Time.

entry.title: Kanye West’s Bully Up for Best Rap Album Grammy
entry.summary: Widespread allegations of A.I. use did not deter voters from nominating Ye’s critically dismissed LP
entry.content:
Kanye West has picked up a Best Rap Album nomination for the deluxe edition of Bully at the 2027 Grammys, where he will face off against Cardi B and Don Toliver, among others. The nod comes despite persistent allegations that Ye had a helping hand in its composition: artificial intelligence.

Speculation stirred after a 2025 interview with Justin Laboy, in which Ye was palpably impressed by the creative possibilities of the technology. He demonstrated its ease in making soundalike vocals, a gimmick likely in evidence on a song premiered later that year with an apparent Ye verse rapped in Spanish, as The New Yorker’s Kelefa Sanneh noted. But Ye subsequently tweeted that the album would feature no A.I., and the claim has not been disproven, despite the efforts of armchair detectives. A lawsuit filed in August upped the stakes, claiming Ye had used A.I. vocal effects in both Vultures 2 and Bully. The Recording Academy rules allow artists to use A.I. provided the human authorship element is “meaningful” and “relevant to the category.”

Ye has a storied history in the Best Rap Album category, having claimed it for each of his first three albums and again for My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy. This is his ninth nomination in the category. As well as Cardi’s Am I the Drama? and Toliver’s Octane, Bully is up against Rapsody’s God Gotta Afro & Gold Hoops, Wale’s Everything Is a Lot, and Busta Rhymes’ latest album set to posthumous J Dilla beats, Dillagence II.

Follow along with all of Pitchfork’s Grammys 2027 coverage.

entry.title: Geese Earn First Grammy Nominations
entry.summary: Including Best New Artist and Best Alternative Music Album
entry.content:
Could a psyop do this? Geese have received their first-ever Grammy nominations, bringing in five nods total. The indie rockers are up for Best New Artist, Best Alternative Music Album (for Getting Killed), Best Rock Performance and Best Rock Song (for “Trinidad”), and Best Alternative Music Performance (for “Au Pays du Cocaine”).

The New York band will duke it out in the Best New Artist category against polka-dotted math rockers Angine de Poitrine, pop phenom Slayyyter, country star Ella Langley, and rapper Don Toliver. They’re also going head to head with Angine de Poitrine for Best Rock Performance and Best Alternative Music Performance. Rounding out the former category are the Rolling Stones, Phoebe Bridgers, and Olivia Rodrigo and Robert Smith for their duet “What’s Wrong With Me.” The latter category includes Bridgers, Rosalía, and Hayley Williams.

Geese’s nominations cap off a breakout year for the quartet of Cameron Winter, Max Bassin, Emily Green, and Dominic DiGesu, who have spent much of 2026 touring behind Getting Killed. They made their Saturday Night Live debut back in January, and won International Group of the Year at the BRIT Awards in February. They also released a live album, Live at Third Man Records, in March.

The 2027 Grammy Awards will take place in Los Angeles on Sunday, February 7 at 7 p.m. ET/4 p.m. PT. You can watch along from home via ABC, Disney+, and Hulu, all three of which will provide live coverage of music’s biggest night.

Follow along with all of Pitchfork’s Grammys 2027 coverage.

entry.title: Phoebe Bridgers, Charli XCX, Rosalía, and Geese Face Off for Best Alternative Album Grammy
entry.summary: Alabama Shakes and Gorillaz are also nominated in the category
entry.content:
Nominations for Best Alternative Music Album have been unveiled for the 2027 Grammy Awards. Facing off in the illustrious but ill-defined category are Alabama Shakes (I Must Be Dreaming), Phoebe Bridgers (Lost Weekend), Charli XCX (Music, Fashion, Film), Geese (Getting Killed), Gorillaz (The Mountain), and, for Lux (Complete Works), Rosalía. That is: anything cool that does not obviously fit anywhere else. Many of these artists look set for a big year: Bridgers, Geese, and Rosalía have already picked up multiple nods elsewhere, too.

The 2026 victors in the category were the Cure, who secured their first-ever statuettes this year, for Songs of a Lost World and its single “Alone.”

entry.title: Tinashe, Slayyyter, Underscores Are Officially Grammy Nominees
entry.summary: The first-time hopefuls will face off in the Best Dance/Electronic Recording category
entry.content:
The Best Dance/Electronic Recording category is in surprisingly good shape at the 2027 Grammy Awards, with Slayyyter, Underscores, and—somehow—Tinashe picking up their first-ever nominations. Recognized for “Crank,” “Music,” and “Melatonin,” respectively, the three first-timers are up against Madonna (“I Feel So Free”), Fred Again.. and Jamie T (“Lights Burn Dimmer”), and Tame Impala (“My Old Ways”). Both Tinashe and Slayyyter are also up for Best Dance Pop Recording; Slayyyter will also compete for Best New Artist and Best Dance/Electronic Album. As ever, the Recording Academy’s common-sense committee can’t win ’em all: Popstar did not receive nods in any album categories.

The nominations cap banner years for all three artists, including the fast-rising Underscores, who was vaulted into arenas in support of Charli XCX. A Slayyyter run behind Wor$t Girl in America, meanwhile, took her to Madison Square Garden.

Read Walden Green’s profile Saint Slayyyter, Kieran Press-Reynolds’ The Not-So-Secret History of Underscores, and follow along with all of Pitchfork’s Grammys 2027 coverage.

entry.title: Grammy Nominations 2027: See the Full List Here
entry.summary: Find out who’s up for Record of the Year, Song of the Year, Best New Artist, and more
entry.content:
The 2027 Grammy Awards are coming up fast, and today (November 16), the Recording Academy announced which artists are in the running for trophies. Leading the pack this year is Raye, whose count of 11 nominations—among them the trifecta of Album, Song, and Record of the Year—ties Beyonce’s 2025 record for the most nominations for a female artist in one year. Close behind is Rosalía with nine nominations behind her 2025 album Lux; she is a first-time nominee in every category she’s up for this year, including Record and Song of the Year. Ella Langley, whose smash “Choosing Texas” became the longest-running No. 1 on the Hot 100 in history this year, has seven nominations, which ties her with her “Choosin Texas’’ co-songwriter Miranda Lambert, Olivia Rodrigo, and Phoebe Bridgers.

The Album of the Year race features Bridgers’ Lost Weekend, Rodrigo’s You Seem Pretty Sad For a Girl So in Love, Langley’s Dandelion, Rosalía’s Lux, and Taylor Swift’s The Life of a Showgirl; rounding out the top-line category are Raye’s This Music May Contain Hope, Olivia Dean’s The Art of Loving, and Bruno Mars’ The Romantic. Many of those artists double up in Song of the Year: Bridgers’ “Lost Boys,” Rodrigo’s “The Cure,” Raye’s “Where Is My Husband?,” Mars’ “Risk It All,” Rosalía’s “Berghain,” and Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas” are all represented, while Ariana Grande picked up a nod for her Petal lead single “Hate That I Made You Love Me.” Swift is in the running, too—not for a TLOAS track, but for “I Knew It, I Knew You,” her original song for Toy Story 5. It’s also up for Best Song Written for Visual Media, a category that includes Andrew Bird’s single for The Pitt and Charli XCX and John Cale’s Wuthering Heights track “House.”

It’s also shaping up to be a big year for first-time nominees. Underscores picked up a nod for Best Dance/Electronic Recording, and Slayyyter and Tinashe both received nominations in the same category, as well as Best Dance Pop Recording. Slayyyter is also nominated for Best Dance/Electronic Album for Wor$t Girl in America. On the other end of the spectrum, Madonna brought her career nominations to 32 with four nominations for Confessions II. The original Confessions on a Dance Floor won Best Electronic/Dance Album Category at the 2007 Grammys.

Next year’s show marks the first time Disney+ will air the event, taking over for longtime host CBS. It will also air live on ABC and Hulu as part of the partnership. Winners will be announced during the ceremony on Sunday, February 7 at 7 p.m. ET/4 p.m. PT.

Last year’s Grammys saw big wins for Bad Bunny, Lady Gaga, Clipse, the Cure, Nine Inch Nails, and FKA twigs, plus an all-star tribute to the late Ozzy Osbourne. A number of winners also took the opportunity to protest the actions of ICE. Joni Mitchell wore an ICE Out pin while accepting Best Historical Recording during the pre-show, and Olivia Dean showed love to her immigrant grandmother in her Best New Artist acceptance speech. Bad Bunny, accepting Best Música Urbana Album for eventual Album of the Year winner Debí Tirar Más Fotos, didn’t mince words, saying, “Before I say thanks to God, I’m going to say ICE out. We are not savage, we are not animals, we are not aliens, we are humans, and we are Americans.”

entry.title: Watch Phoebe Bridgers Play “Bobby” and “Still Standing” on Saturday Night Live
entry.summary: The singer-songwriter made her third SNL appearance, this time to promote Lost Weekend
entry.content:
A lot has changed since Phoebe Bridgers’ stint as a guitar-smashing musical guest on Saturday Night Live in 2021, notably her arena-headlining status as a solo act and another SNL appearance with the Grammy-dominating supergroup Boygenius. Last night (November 14), Bridgers visited Saturday Night Live yet again, this time to perform two songs from Lost Weekend: “Bobby” and “Still Standing.” Watch a replay below.

Joining Bridgers for the live rendition of “Bobby” was a full backing band, including Melina Duterte of Jay Som on guitar, and an eerie pooling of smoke by their feet. During “Still Standing,” Bridgers performed onstage alone in a white lace dress and simple makeup — normally unremarkable, except that during the final stretch of the song, black lights revealed she was actually wearing skeleton face paint.

Bridgers heads to Europe next month to continue her shows in support of Lost Weekend. She recently announced that tour is getting extended through 2027, including a bunch of new dates in North America with Paper Wings and her longtime collaborator Christian Lee Hutson.

Last month, Bridgers dropped a Tidal-exclusive live EP of songs from her new album, as recorded at Madison Square Garden. She’s also kept quite busy as an actor, starring in a nuanced role in Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime (for which she also chipped in an original song) and voice acting roles in short films by My Chemical Romance and Conor Oberst.

Read Hattie Lindert’s concert review Going Analog at Phoebe Bridgers’ Phones-Free MSG Show.

entry.title: Peter Hook, Lauren Mayberry, Deftones Play Joy Division and New Order Songs at 2026 Rock Hall
entry.summary: They christened the 2026 induction ceremony with “Love Will Tear Us Apart” and “Bizarre Love Triangle”
entry.content:
Last night (November 14), the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame 2026 induction ceremony took place at Los Angeles’ Peacock Theater, where Joy Division and New Order were simultaneously honored, with Trent Reznor handling their induction speech. Given the band members’ decades-long feud, only Hook showed up to the event. He was joined by Deftones to perform Joy Division’s eternal hit “Love Will Tear Us Apart,” with Chino Moreno handling lead vocals, and then Chvrches’ Lauren Mayberry took over on the mic for New Order’s “Bizarre Love Triangle.” Watch footage of their performance below.

“I’m on my own, but I’m not alone,” Hook said during his acceptance speech on behalf of both bands. “For me, it’s been a wild 50 years. I’ve been happy, I’ve been mad, I’ve been heartbroken in equal measures, but I’m still fucking here. Music is eternal, fans are eternal, and we are eternally grateful.” Hook did not mention his former bandmates by name at any point or thank them, apart from Joy Division’s late singer, Ian Curtis.

Joy Division and New Order are, of course, two different bands, but they were nominated as a package deal twice in the past, in 2023 and 2025, before earning the official selection in 2026. Their bundling makes sense considering Joy Division’s surviving members formed New Order after Curtis died in 1980. Hook’s beef with New Order is infamous. He left the band in 2007 and then spent years in a legal battle over royalties with his former bandmates. He previously said he wouldn’t appear at the induction ceremony’s podium with the group unless they apologized to him, and that he would be willing to perform together again if they did. Looks like the reunion bets are off.

This year, the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony was not live streamed. Instead, fans can tune in to watch a broadcast of the event on ABC and Disney+ on December 8. This other 2026 inductees were Oasis, Phil Collins, Iron Maiden, Wu-Tang Clan, Sade, Billy Idol, and Luther Vandross. The Early Influence Award was handed out to Fela Kuti, Queen Latifah, MC Lyte, and Gram Parsons this year. Meanwhile, the Musical Excellence Awards went to Linda Creed and Rick Rubin, among others, while the late Ed Sullivan honored with the 2026 Ahmet Ertegun Award for non-artists.
